PCRMs logo: the enhancer loop as a cursive P, made of DNA

A strand of DNA writes a script P. It enters from the left, crosses the stem, sweeps round the bowl (the enhancer loop), runs down the stem and ends in the gene’s start arrow. Where it crosses the stem, transcription factors bring the enhancer and promoter together. Each version is shown on its own, on the tile, at 32 and 16px, standing in for the P in “PCRMs”, and beside the name.

P1 Double helix

A double helix writes the P, with base pairs between the strands and proper over-and-under crossings. One key TF sits where the strand crosses the stem.
